title: How do we expand brackets with three terms in them?
description: Two expressions, each with a bracket of three terms, are multiplied out term by term. Like terms are added, and both results are checked by putting numbers back in.
teaching_notes: One idea: every term multiplies every term, then the like terms are added. Same method as the bracket of two terms times a bracket of three terms in your book.

video_script.why: The child has multiplied a bracket of two terms by a bracket of three. Here the sizes and the signs are new.
video_script.substitution: Multiply every term by every term, write all the pieces, and add the like terms.
video_script.anchor: the two expressions, each with a bracket of three terms
video_script.payoff_line: Multiply every term, then add the like terms

final_answer.spoken: the first is four eigh, plus five eigh b, plus eigh b squared, minus twelve b squared, minus three b cubed

maths_rules: 4ab and ab are like terms: 4ab + ab = 5ab, so 4a + 5ab + ab² − 12b² − 3b³
check the second with y = 1, z = 1: 11 × 9 = 99 and 4 + 44 − 5 + 77 − 21 = 99
video_script.design: One idea: every term multiplies every term, then like terms are added. Uses the method of the six pieces video. The two expressions stay on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two expressions are on the board. Each one has a bracket with three terms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we expand both of them?

beats.on_screen: the two expressions stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: arrows from each term of one bracket to each term of the other; beside it, ab and 4ab lit with the words like terms = same letter numbers

marks.all: arrows run from each term of one bracket to each term of the other

narration: <bookmark mark='all'/>Every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other.
<bookmark mark='like'/>Pieces with the same letter numbers are called like terms, and they can be added.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two expressions, each a bracket times a bracket.

beats.on_screen: To find: both expanded and simplified

marks.find: the words expanded and simplified are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to expand both and simplify them.

beats.on_screen: (a + ab − 3b²)(4 + b): × 4 gives 4a + 4ab − 12b²; × b gives ab + ab² − 3b³

marks.q2: a × b = ab, ab × b = ab² and (−3b²) × b = −3b³ are written

beats.colours: the four pieces and the b pieces in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='q1'/>Step one, multiply each term of the first bracket by four.
That gives four eigh, four eigh b, and negative twelve b squared.
<bookmark mark='q2'/>Then multiply each term by b.
That gives eigh b, eigh b squared, and negative three b cubed.

beats.on_screen: 4ab + ab = 5ab; no other like terms; (i) has 5 terms: 4a, 5ab, ab², −12b², −3b³

marks.l2: the other pieces 4a, ab², −12b² and −3b³ are listed as having different letter numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='l1'/>Step two, look for like terms. Four eigh b and eigh b have the same letter numbers, so they add to five eigh b.
<bookmark mark='l2'/>No other pieces are like terms, so the first result has five terms.
<bookmark mark='r1'/>Step three, take the second expression. Four y times y is four y squared. Four y times eleven z is forty four y z.
<bookmark mark='r2'/>Four y times negative three is negative twelve y, and seven times y is seven y.
<bookmark mark='r3'/>Seven times eleven z is seventy seven z, and seven times negative three is negative twenty one.

beats.colours: the two y pieces in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Step four, look for like terms. Negative twelve y and seven y are like terms.
They add to negative five y.
<bookmark mark='k2'/>No other pieces are like terms, so the second result has five terms.

beats.on_screen: check the first with a = 1, b = 1: (1 + 1 − 3)(4 + 1) = −5 and 4 + 5 + 1 − 12 − 3 = −5; check the second with y = 1, z = 1: 11 × 9 = 99 and 4 + 44 − 5 + 77 − 21 = 99
narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step five, check both. For the first, put eigh as one and b as one.
The original gives negative one times five, which is negative five.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>The result gives four, plus five, plus one, minus twelve, minus three, which is negative five too.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>For the second, put y as one and z as one. The original gives eleven times nine, which is ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='c4'/>The result gives four, plus forty four, minus five, plus seventy seven, minus twenty one.
That is ninety nine too.

marks.pay: the words multiply every term, then add the like terms appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Multiply every term, then add the like terms.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The first is four eigh, plus five eigh b, plus eigh b squared.
Then minus twelve b squared, minus three b cubed.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The second is four y squared, plus forty four y z, minus five y.
Then plus seventy seven z, minus twenty one.
